the calculation of hadronic matrix elements for two-body charmless B decays, and with the evaluation of the corresponding branching fractions and CP-violation asymmetries.
the calculation of the hadronic matrix element of the 4-fermion operator O(μ) in terms of decay constants and form-factors.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the naive factorization hypothesis, which is based on the OPE and the vacuum saturation approximation, is a reasonable approximation to describe hadronic two-body charmless B decays, but it is not exact, and it is not a good approximation to describe the scale dependence of the factorized amplitudes.
the factorization hypothesis is not a fundamental assumption, but a calculational tool.

the naive factorization hypothesis works very well for B decays, and it is not necessary to go beyond the naive factorization to understand the observed B decay rates and the branching ratios for B decays into two-body final states.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have studied the scale and scheme dependences of the hadronic matrix element under the naive factorization hypothesis and have shown that the scale and scheme ambiguities of the naive factorized amplitudes can be absorbed by the redefinition of the decay constants and the form factors in a consistent manner.
the factorization approach is not reliable in charmless B decays and the full QCD calculations are needed.

we have shown the existence of the scale and scheme ambiguities with naive factorization and that we have proposed a new scheme, called the modified perturbative QCD (MPQCD) scheme, in which the scale and γ5 scheme ambiguities are removed and the scheme dependence is greatly reduced.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the factorization hypothesis is not sufficient to ensure renormalization scale and scheme independence in charmless B decays.

the naive factorization is not a good approximation to the full hadronic matrix elements and it is not possible to make a reliable prediction of hadronic two-body charmless B decays using this approximation.
, while the naive factorization is a useful tool for estimating the hadronic matrix element in the absence of first principles calculations, it should not be taken as the final word on the subject.
